title: feat(types,plugin-kanban,sdui-parser)!: retire `quickAdd` on object-kanban and stop forwarding it (objectui#8285)
body:
Fixes #8285
Clause-②: yes

objectui's half of ruling B (director seat, decision batch #91, comment 5583979207): "The board does not grow an inline record-creation write path", `object-kanban.quickAdd` is retired, and objectui stops forwarding it. `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 (installed since objectui#11086) already carries the spec half as a `retiredKey(...)` tombstone. The `Clause-②: yes` line is copied from the claim (comment 5912959131): the published `@object-ui/types` face narrows, and the `inert-quick-add` code leaves `@object-ui/sdui-parser`'s diagnostic payload.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/types`**: `ObjectKanbanSchema.quickAdd` is now `?: never` (TypeScript face) and `retirementTombstone(...)` (zod mirror). An authored value is refused BY NAME (`invalid_type` at `quickAdd`, with the remedy), not stripped. I used the existing tombstone helper; no new helper. The `onQuickAdd` docblock is rewritten because this change made its old wording false. See the open question below.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-kanban`**: `ObjectKanban` stops forwarding `quickAdd`. Its `effectiveSchema` now carries `quickAdd: undefined`. `KanbanRenderer` is byte-identical. The `OBJECT_KANBAN_INPUTS` docblock now records the retirement instead of the "PREMATURE" carve-out.
- **`@object-ui/sdui-parser`**: I deleted the interim `kanban-quick-add.ts` module, its wiring in `validate.ts` and its four barrel exports. The references to the deleted symbol in `body-dialect.ts` and its test are removed too.
- **Pins**: I rewrote the tripwire, renamed `quickAddIsDiagnosedNotDropped-8285.test.ts` to `quickAddRetiredNotForwarded-8285.test.tsx`. I rewrote `kanban-quick-add-8285.test.ts` for the new state and added `object-kanban-quick-add-retired-8285.test.ts`. The 8801 and 8802 pins used `quickAdd: true` as a "live member" control, so it is removed from those lists.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx` and `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`. Both passages said the key "still parses" and that the tier answers `inert-quick-add`, and both are false after this change. Only prose changed; no fenced block moved.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/8285-object-kanban-quick-add-retired.md`, `minor` ×3 with BREAKING wording and a migration section. Per objectui's version rule, a breaking change is `minor`, never `major`.

## The premises, measured (dispatch Zone 2)

1. **Spec tombstone: confirmed.** In the worktree's `node_modules/@objectstack/spec` (17.5.0), `ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban'].quickAdd` is a `retiredKey(...)`. Parsing `{ objectName, quickAdd: true }` gives `success=false` with one issue: `code=invalid_type`, `path=["quickAdd"]`, `keys=undefined`, and a message that starts "`object-kanban` property `quickAdd` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17 (ADR-0049)". `quickAdd: false` is refused the same way. Controls on the same call: `bogusProp` gives `unrecognized_keys` with `keys=["bogusProp"]`, and `{ objectName }` alone gives `success=true`.
2. **Why the tripwire stayed green: the helper read one issue shape only.** The old `refusedByName` collected `issue.keys`. zod fills `keys` only on `unrecognized_keys`. A tombstone declares the key as `never`, so its refusal is `invalid_type` at the key's path with no `keys`. The helper therefore returned `[]` whether the spec published the key or retired it. The row's `bogusProp` control is an `unrecognized_keys` issue, so it could not fail for the reason the row was meant to catch. On the base commit, the two 8285 files ran 18/18 green with the key already retired. The new `refusedByName` reads both shapes and has a control for each.
3. **Tags: one, not two.** `object-kanban` is the only `ComponentRegistry.register(...)` call for `ObjectKanbanRenderer`. `kanban` retired with objectui#8802 and `kanban-ui` with objectui#8257, and both read `has() === false` in the new row 5. `kanban-ui`'s Quick Add pair now lives on the exported `KanbanRenderer` component, and `ObjectKanban` also renders that component. So I cut the key upstream, in `ObjectKanban`, where the `schema` that `KanbanRenderer` reads is built. Every `object-kanban` entry point goes through `ObjectKanban`: the tag, the published `kanbanComponents['object-kanban']` map and a host mounting `ObjectKanban` directly. Cutting only in `ObjectKanbanRenderer`, the file the claim names, would have missed the map. The tombstone text names `KanbanRenderer`, not a `kanban-ui` tag, because a document naming that tag is now an `unknown-component` error.
4. **Zod member: done with the neighbours' construct.** `retirementTombstone()` is what the `groupField` and `allowCollapse` members next to it use.
5. **Html tier: I deleted the interim diagnostic.** The same `validateTree` probe over an `object-kanban` manifest gives, **with** the module: `quickAdd=true` produces `warning / inert-quick-add`, and `quickAdd=false` falls through to `warning / unknown-prop` ("has no prop quickAdd"). **Without** it, both produce `warning / unknown-prop`, and `compile()` stays `ok=true`. That message is now true on every face: the spec, both `@object-ui/types` faces, the registry inputs and the renderer. On this tier it is also the whole remedy, because a constrained-JSX page cannot write the handler, so deleting the key is the only edit open to its author. The retired `body` dialect keeps its own replacement diagnostic for a different reason: it has a replacement spelling (`children`) to name. `quickAdd` has none. Severity is unchanged (warning), so no page that saves today stops saving.

## Measurements

All runs are at head `5218c1fa1a` (this branch with `main` merged at `dded788ada`), and heavy ones went through the shared verify lock. Exit codes were captured before any pipe.

- Build: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-kanban^...' --concurrency=2`, 12/12 tasks successful. This includes `@object-ui/sdui-parser`'s own `check-dist-completeness`.
- Type-check: `pnpm --filter X type-check` gives exit 0 for `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` and `@object-ui/sdui-parser`. All three new or rewritten test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` programs (`--listFiles`, 1 hit each), so the type-level pins really run.
- Tests: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/ packages/sdui-parser/ packages/types/`, plus a 16-file sweep. The sweep is the console registry↔spec ledger, `public-contract`, the handler-key and doc-type script tests, the schema-catalog corpora, and the cli validate, app-shell block-config, plugin-view and plugin-list consumers of the `object-kanban` arm, and the doc readers. Result: **391 files, 8375 tests passed**, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check-changeset-presence` (15 source files of 3 released packages, 1 changeset), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:self-import`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`. The governed-surface guard says NOT GOVERNED.
- ESLint, narrowed and declared: the 13 changed TS/TSX files, 0 errors. The population is the config's own `**/*.{ts,tsx}` blocks, and the count of 13 comes from `--format json`. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. Warnings on the four edited source files are identical to base, 31/23/34/1.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples` exit 2 (PRECONDITION NOT MET, they need a broad build), but no fenced line changed in the docs diff (0 lines). `check:sdui-registration-pins` and `check:readme-exports` need console and whole-tree builds and were not run. This diff adds or changes no registration, and no README names the four removed exports.

Ablations, each done through `ablation-replace.mjs` with an on-disk anchor count and blob-hash proof, and restored to `blob == HEAD` with an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- **Remove the `quickAdd: undefined` cut.** The renderer pin's row 1 goes red (`expected [ button …, … ] to have a length of +0 but got 2`, one control per lane). The other 4 rows stay green, row 2 included. That row is the control: the same query finds the host pair's control.
- **Turn the zod tombstone back into a boolean.** 3 rows go red (both refusal rows, and the describe-channel row) and 3 stay green (still declared, near miss, bare node), as predicted.
- **Type reverse check.** A `quickAdd: true` literal typed `ObjectKanbanSchema`, planted in `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` against the rebuilt `@object-ui/types` dist, fails with `TS2322: Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'undefined'`. My first attempt was a no-op that the tool refused: the replacement contained the anchor, so the count did not drop and tsc never ran. I re-anchored it and ran it again.

## Open question: `onQuickAdd` on `object-kanban` (not settled here)

With `quickAdd` retired and no longer forwarded, `ObjectKanbanSchema.onQuickAdd` still reaches the board by identity; the `handlerKeyDispositionsMeasured-7804` and `kanban-handler-slots-7664` pins still hold. But the board never calls it, because the control needs both halves. Retiring it too would need a `?: never` tombstone and a `'retired'` disposition. `check:handler-key-reads` refuses that while a renderer still reads the key off the document, and its static walk reaches `KanbanRenderer`'s `schema.onQuickAdd` read through `ObjectKanban`. So the read on the `ObjectKanban` path would first have to move off `KanbanRenderer`'s `schema`, without changing the host pair. The ruling names `quickAdd` only, so I left the slot as it is and wrote the question into the card report.

## Cross-repo consequence (not filed)

objectstack keeps its own copy of this parser, and its `objectui-lockstep.json` still lists `inert-quick-add`, recorded against objectui `db11afd4967c`. At objectstack's next `.objectui-sha` bump, `check:sdui-lockstep` will name that code as present on one side only, and their copy should drop it the same way. That is the lockstep working as designed, so I have noted it rather than filed it.

## Acceptance notes

- `index.tsx`'s `OBJECT_KANBAN_INPUTS` docblock still says "both `ObjectKanbanRenderer` tags" in its heading. That has been stale since objectui#8802 and this change does not touch it. Noted, not fixed.
